title: 2022 HMMT November Guts Problem 28
statement: Let \(A B C\) be a triangle with \(A B=13, B C=14\), and \(C A=15\). Pick points \(Q\) and \(R\) on \(A C\) and \(A B\) such that \(\angle C B Q=\angle B C R=90^{\circ}\). There exist two points \(P_{1} \neq P_{2}\) in the plane of \(A B C\) such that \(\triangle P_{1} Q R, \triangle P_{2} Q R\), and \(\triangle A B C\) are similar (with vertices in order). Compute the sum of the distances from \(P_{1}\) to \(B C\) and \(P_{2}\) to \(B C\).

solutions.text:
As in the previous solution, let \(T\) be the foot from \(A\) to \(B C\), let \(T^{\prime}\) be the foot from \(P\) to \(Q R\). and recall that

\[d\left(P_{1}, B C\right)+d\left(P_{2}, B C\right)=2 d\left(T^{\prime}, B C\right)\]

Now, notice that since \(\triangle P Q R \sim \triangle A B C\), we have \(Q T^{\prime}: T^{\prime} R=B T: T C\), so \(T T^{\prime}\|B Q\| C R\), implying that \(A \in T T^{\prime}\).
However, we recall a well-known fact that \(A\) is the midpoint of \(T T^{\prime}\) (can be proven by simple similar triangles). Thus, \(d\left(T^{\prime}, B C\right)\) is equal to two times the altitude from \(A\) to \(B C\). Hence, the answer is four times the altitude from \(A\) to \(B C\), which is 48 .
